Policy_Purpose: Defra's Environmental Indicator Framework (formerly the Outcome Indicator Framework) tracks environmental change in England against the ten goals of the Environmental Improvement Plan, the statutory plan required under the Environment Act 2021. Its indicators form the evidence base for Defra's annual EIP progress report, which the Office for Environmental Protection scrutinises independently. Coverage is deliberately broad — air, water, land, seas, wildlife, resource efficiency, biosecurity and people's engagement with nature — rather than biodiversity alone.

Policy_Purpose: The Climate Change Committee's mitigation monitoring framework supports its statutory duty under the Climate Change Act 2008 to report annually to Parliament on UK progress in reducing emissions. It tracks emissions against the legally binding five-year carbon budgets on the path to net zero by 2050, and does so through indicators of the underlying drivers - deployment rates, technology uptake, demand and market activity - rather than emissions alone. The framework was published in June 2025 and updated in June 2026. Its benchmark is the Government's Carbon Budget and Growth Delivery Plan (October 2025), which replaced the Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023, supplemented by the CCC's Balanced Pathway where no government target exists. Scope is economy-wide across the CCC's eleven sectors: surface transport, buildings, electricity supply, industry, agriculture and land use, fuel supply, waste, aviation, shipping, F-gases and engineered removals. CURRENCY NOTE: all 79 rows are benchmarked against the Carbon Budget and Growth Delivery Plan (29 October 2025, updated 23 June 2026) and the CCC Progress in reducing emissions 2026 report, re-derived in indicators v18-v20. No row now carries a superseded or unverified benchmark.

Policy_Purpose: The Climate Change Committee's adaptation monitoring framework supports its statutory duty under the Climate Change Act 2008 to report to Parliament on UK progress in adapting to climate change, and its parallel duties under devolved climate legislation. It was rebuilt in May 2026 on the evidence of the Fourth Independent Assessment of UK Climate Risk (CCRA4-IA), replacing the 2023-2025 framework held as [IFW-11]. Monitoring is organised around fourteen systems - health; built environment and communities; public services; cultural heritage; water and wastewater; energy; transport; waste; digital and telecoms; land; sea; food security; economy and finance; and national security and international engagement - each with a published monitoring map of objective, targets, actions, enablers and policies. WHAT IS HELD: the framework publishes no indicator list, because the CCC selects indicators against these targets in each adaptation progress report. The 38 records here are therefore the framework's PROPOSED TARGETS, one per target, which are the measurable, time-bound quantities the framework actually publishes. They span all fourteen systems and sit under 20 system objectives; the CCC states 21 objectives in A Well-Adapted UK, and the twentieth and twenty-first are not separately distinguishable on the published system pages.

Policy_Purpose: The UK Biodiversity Indicators are an accredited official statistics compendium produced by JNCC and Defra, giving an annual snapshot of the status of UK biodiversity and how it is changing. They serve two reporting purposes. Internationally, they are the UK's principal evidence for national reporting to the Convention on Biological Diversity, and the 2025 suite was revised specifically to align with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework ahead of the 2026 and 2029 national reports. Domestically, the parallel England suite feeds Defra's Environmental Indicator Framework. Coverage spans species and habitat status, the pressures acting on them, ecosystem services, and enabling conditions such as finance, data and public engagement.

Policy_Purpose: State of Nature is a periodic assessment of UK wildlife produced by a partnership of more than 60 conservation NGOs, research institutes and statutory nature conservation bodies, drawing on biological recording and monitoring data collected largely by volunteers. It is not a government reporting framework and carries no statutory targets: its purpose is to provide an independent benchmark for the status of UK species and habitats, to set that against the pressures acting on nature, and to assess the conservation responses being made. The 2023 edition reports UK-level trends with separate summaries for England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

Policy_Purpose: The Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, adopted at CBD COP15 in December 2022, sets four goals for 2050 and 23 targets for 2030 on a pathway to the Convention's vision of living in harmony with nature. The targets divide into three groups: reducing threats to biodiversity (1–8), meeting people's needs through sustainable use and benefit-sharing (9–13), and tools for implementation and mainstreaming (14–23). The accompanying monitoring framework, finalised at COP16, defines headline, component, binary and complementary indicators against which all Parties — the UK among them — report at least every five years.

Policy_Purpose: IPBES is the intergovernmental science-policy platform tasked with assessing the state of knowledge on biodiversity and ecosystem services for decision-makers. The 2019 Global Assessment, compiled by 145 expert authors from a systematic review of around 15,000 scientific and government sources and drawing for the first time at this scale on indigenous and local knowledge, assessed five decades of change in nature, its contributions to people, and the causes behind them. The indicators drawn from it characterise the five direct drivers of biodiversity loss — land- and sea-use change, direct exploitation of species, climate change, pollution and invasive alien species — together with the indirect economic and demographic drivers behind them. Its role is to inform policy, not to set or track targets.

Policy_Purpose: The global indicator framework for the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development was developed by the Inter-agency and Expert Group on SDG Indicators and adopted by the UN General Assembly in resolution A/RES/71/313. It is the statistical apparatus for monitoring progress, informing policy and holding stakeholders accountable across the 17 Goals and 169 targets, and is refined annually with comprehensive reviews by the UN Statistical Commission — most recently in 2025. The framework spans the full social, economic and environmental agenda; the records held here are the nature- and climate-relevant subset.

Policy_Purpose: The European Environment Agency maintains the indicator set used to monitor Europe's progress on biodiversity and ecosystem health, principally against the EU Biodiversity Strategy for 2030 and the 8th Environment Action Programme, with the EU Biodiversity Strategy dashboard as the main reporting vehicle. The indicators cover the conservation status of species and habitats under the Habitats Directive, protected-area coverage towards the 30% land and sea target, ecosystem extent and condition, and the pressures of land-use change, pollution and climate change. Several double as EU-level reporting for SDG 14 and SDG 15, and the Nature Restoration Regulation (EU 2024/1991) adds restoration-progress reporting to the same set.
